security_spec.violation_condition: In the FreeBSD kernel, if/when AIA IMSIC/ACLIC support is implemented (currently unsupported in mainline — sys/riscv/riscv/aplic.c:456-457 explicitly disallows IMSIC pairing), code that writes xithreshold (via miselect/siselect indirect CSR access) and then checks preemption using the old precedence rule `iprio[i] & NIPPRIO_MASK >= xithreshold` would incorrectly treat the masked-priority-vs-threshold comparison as a boolean-AND between iprio[i] and (NIPPRIO_MASK >= xithreshold), causing high-priority interrupts to potentially be spuriously masked or low-priority interrupts to incorrectly preempt critical sections.
security_spec.summary: FreeBSD currently only supports APLIC direct mode (no IMSIC/ACLIC), so this ACLIC spec-level operator-precedence bug in the xithreshold preemption gate has no current code impact, but any future AIA/IMSIC implementation that follows the old spec would have broken priority-based interrupt preemption logic.

findings.finding: APLIC is configured in direct mode only; IMSIC pairing is explicitly rejected (line 455-458). ITHRESHOLD is disabled for all CPUs. Smnip/Ssnip requires IMSIC/ACLIC (Smaia), which is unsupported, so the NIPPRIO_MASK/threshold precedence bug cannot manifest.

spec_citations.excerpt: The Smnip extension depends on the Smaia extension and adds nested preemption support at machine level. The Ssnip extension depends on the Smnip extension and adds nested preemption support at supervisor level.

A mask for filtering out the bits of a priority number that will participate in the selection for nested interrupt preemption is: NIPPRIO_MASK = ~(2^(mipreemptcfg.preemptmsk) - 1) ... The condition for threshold masking: IPRIO >= xithreshold & NIPPRIO_MASK

findings.finding: VMM APLIC ITHRESHOLD register is listed as accessible for guest MMIO but is not actually emulated (read/write pass-through with no state tracking). No Smnip/mithreshold/sithreshold CSR virtualization exists anywhere in the hypervisor. No Smnip-specific indirect CSR access (miselect/siselect) is implemented.

Explicit guard: APLIC with IMSIC on hart is not supported. Since Smnip requires Smaia/IMSIC infrastructure, the entire attack surface (mithreshold/sithreshold CSRs, miselect/siselect indirect CSR access, NIPPRIO_MASK-based preemption) is absent.

spec_citations.excerpt: Smnip: Nested Interrupt Preemption support at Machine level
